Question B-003-016-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Series batteries add voltage while capacity stays the same, so two 12 V, 20 Ah batteries become 24 V, 20 Ah.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "24 volts, 20 ampere-hours": This is the correct choice because series batteries add voltage while capacity stays the same, so two 12 V, 20 Ah batteries become 24 V, 20 Ah.
- sourceIndex 1: "24 volts, 40 ampere-hours": This adds capacity as if the batteries were in parallel, but series keeps ampere-hours the same.
- sourceIndex 2: "12 volts, 40 ampere-hours": This is the parallel result: voltage unchanged and capacity doubled.
- sourceIndex 3: "6 volts, 80 ampere-hours": This would require a different converter or arrangement; two equal batteries in series do not halve voltage or quadruple capacity.
